Studies were excluded if they lacked measurable prevention outcomes or sufficient methodological detail, or focused on injury treatment rather than prevention, to ensure relevant and interpretable evidence for synthesis. Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. ML models generally outperformed or matched traditional screening methods for self-harm and suicide prediction (AUC 0.81-0.82), while multimodal approaches achieved the highest predictive accuracy (AUC 0.90). In abuse and violence prevention, AI predicted intimate partner violence with an AUC of 0.88 and identified cases before formal disclosure. AI also improved fall risk assessment by accurately categorizing patient risk levels, predicting future falls, and mitigating fall injuries through wearable airbag technology. ML models predicted future sports-related injuries (AUC 0.76-0.84), while identifying modifiable risk factors including workload, strength deficits, prior injury burden, and concussion history. ML-based prediction showed promise for risk stratification in self-harm, suicide, intimate partner violence, and recurrent victimization. Additionally, AI predicted fall risk and identified athletes at risk for future sports-related injuries while detecting modifiable risk factors, including workload, prior injury burden, and strength deficits. Although these findings suggest that AI and ML may have potential applications in supporting earlier risk identification, informing targeted prevention strategies, and facilitating more personalized approaches to injury prevention, the limited available evidence warrants careful interpretation.

title: Preceding organ trajectories guide dynamic reassessment after apparent stabilisation in sepsis
desc: Apparent organ recovery can conceal residual vulnerability in sepsis. Across 19,690 adults in four intensive care databases, we evaluated six-hour deterioration in low-severity organs after transition to single-organ dysfunction. At 2,492 eICU reassessment alerts, adding preceding organ trajectories increased capture from 219 to 282 episodes (28.8%; difference 63, 95% CI 38.0 to 93.5). Reassessment depended on the availability and updating of that history. Withholding half of record batches lost 108.3 captures; adaptation recovered approximately one third, and targeted retrieval increased timely correct nominations from 151 to 163. New measurements modified the value of earlier history, while local calibration and alert scheduling improved external reassessment. Among 813 norepinephrine-treated patients, history improved hypotension-or-death discrimination (AUROC 0.5925 to 0.6929) and, in the fixed-model comparison, concentrated larger estimated recorded exposure reductions across treatment priorities (AUTOC difference 25.68 micrograms/kg, 95% CI 5.23 to 46.16). These findings support retaining organ trajectories for dynamic reassessment and treatment prioritisation.

title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models
desc: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have created opportunities for cross-lingual transfer of medical knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages to support access to healthcare information. However, medical question-answering (QA) datasets for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs remain scarce for Tetun. To address this gap, we translated MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information collections into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 medical QA pairs. Translation quality was assessed on 50 randomly sampled QA pairs (100 documents) using automatic metrics against human reference translations and evaluations by two native Tetun-speaking healthcare professionals, focusing on medical accuracy and Tetun fluency. Human translations achieved higher mean ratings than LLM-generated translations for both criteria (4.43/5 vs. 4.02/5), with statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To assess downstream utility, we fine-tuned Gemma and Llama variants on the translated MedAlpaca dataset using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and evaluated them on 325 Tetun-translated United States Medical Licensing Examination multiple-choice questions. Gemma 4 12B fine-tuned using QLoRA achieved relative improvements in mean accuracy of 10.79% with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) inference and 10.42% after merging the LoRA adapters into the BF16 base model, compared with the corresponding base models. These results highlight the viability of automatic dataset translation for Tetun medical QA and the effectiveness of PEFT in enhancing model performance. The datasets, models, and evaluation resources are accessible at https://github.com/labadain/labadain-medqa to support reproducible research on Tetun medical QA and facilitate machine translation, cross lingual, and multilingual research.

title: China's InventisBio delivers competitive TYK2 data in phase 3 psoriasis win
Nanobiomechanics in Oncology: Atomic Force Microscopy for Cancer Mechanophenotyping Using Cellular Young's Modulus.
source: PubMed · Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand
desc: [Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand] This review examines the current literature on the application of atomic force microscopy (AFM) to cancer mechanophenotyping, with particular emphasis on cellular Young's modulus and its potential diagnostic significance. A structured electronic search of PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar was conducted to identify studies published between 1999 and 2025 reporting AFM-based measurements of cellular Young's modulus in cancer-related models. Across multiple malignancies, reduced cellular stiffness is frequently observed in malignant compared with non-malignant cells and is associated with cytoskeletal remodelling, increased deformability and altered cell-matrix interactions. However, the relationship between Young's modulus and malignancy is not universally monotonic. Nanomechanical properties may vary across different pathological states and malignant phenotypes rather than following a simple monotonic trajectory, while invasive and metastatic cells can dynamically remodel their cytoskeleton and modify their stiffness in response to environmental and mechanical constraints. Young's modulus should therefore not be regarded as an isolated universal cancer biomarker, but rather as one component of a dynamic mechanophenotype influenced by disease stage, cellular region, microenvironment and measurement methodology. Recent advances in automated force acquisition, optical cell recognition, artificial intelligence and high-throughput AFM are beginning to address traditional limitations in measurement efficiency and operator dependence. The future diagnostic value of AFM may therefore lie in integrating Young's modulus with complementary parameters, including spatial mechanical heterogeneity, viscoelasticity, adhesion, deformation-energy characteristics and nanotopography, to define multidimensional cancer mechanophenotypes. Standardised acquisition and analysis protocols, together with validation in patient-derived specimens, will be essential for translating AFM nanomechanics from an experimental measurement into a clinically informative biomechanical biomarker.

title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
desc: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance. In this study, we evaluate fourteen current models from six leading providers, one smaller and one larger model from each provider with two additional open-weight models, on 3,076 questions from four medical benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MedBullets) under standard multiple choice, the same questions with the answer choices withheld, and reconstruction of a hidden question from its choices alone. In the standard multiple-choice setting, the strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline on MedQA-USMLE and PubMedQA, but the smaller models trail their larger models by 8.7 percentage points and only two of the six pass the human-expert bar on the licensing examination. Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models. On memorization, the strongest models reconstruct one question in four from the answer choices alone, yet accuracy holds on the questions they cannot reconstruct. We further weigh accuracy against inference cost and test whether ensembling several models improves medical question answering.

title: FDA dims Bright Minds’ outlook with partial hold on seizure trial over toxicity in mice
Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Interpretation in Diagnostic Radiology: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy and Operational Efficiency.
desc: [Cureus] Rising imaging workload and a shortage of radiology specialists have driven interest in artificial intelligence (AI) to improve diagnostic speed and accuracy. This systematic review, without meta-analysis, describes how AI affects diagnostic accuracy and operational efficiency compared with human interpretation in diagnostic radiology. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) and Cochrane guidance, PubMed, ClinicalKey, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched on 11 April 2026 for studies published from January 2019 onwards. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and a Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2)-based risk-of-bias assessment. Twenty-one studies were included: 11 compared standalone AI with human readers, six compared AI-assisted with unassisted readers, and four reported both; 18 evaluated task-specific image-analysis AI and three evaluated generative AI models. Because no subgroup was homogeneous enough to pool, we synthesised results narratively and stratified them by comparison type, AI category, imaging modality, and study quality. Standalone image-analysis AI achieved high sensitivity for fractures and selected chest findings but performed less well on subtle findings and lower-quality images, and in one computed tomography-referenced comparison a radiologist outperformed AI. AI assistance improved reader performance more consistently, particularly among less experienced readers. Generative models did not reach specialist performance on complex tasks. Efficiency gains were concentrated in normal studies, and the only randomised trial found lower mammography screen-reading workload with similar early screening performance. No study assessed patient outcomes, and 18 of 21 studies were retrospective. This evidence supports AI only as a supervised, complementary tool; improvements in diagnostic accuracy should not be equated with clinical benefit.

title: Physiological Trajectories and Observation Patterns in ICU Mortality Prediction: Transportability Under Changing Measurement Conditions
desc: Objective: To distinguish the transferable predictive value of physiological trajectories from that of observation patterns in ICU mortality prediction, and to assess whether measurement timing affects performance independently of observation quantity. Materials and Methods: In-hospital mortality was predicted at 48 hours using MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. Nested representations progressively integrated latest-value snapshots (R1), longitudinal physiological summaries (R2), and measurement frequency and timing features (R3). Models fitted on 7,762 MetaVision patients were evaluated on 21,682 MIMIC-IV patients and 43,878 eICU patients across 204 hospitals. The effect of measurement timing was assessed while holding the number of retained observations constant. Results: Physiological trajectories improved external prediction in eICU (R2-R1 log-loss difference -0.00922, 95% CI -0.01148 to -0.00704). Observation-pattern features improved locally developed eICU models (R3-R2 -0.00257, 95% CI -0.00370 to -0.00146), but not clearly after transfer from MetaVision (-0.00012, 95% CI -0.00206 to +0.00208). R3 was favoured in 10 of 30 source bootstrap refits. At matched observation counts, retaining measurements spread throughout the window reduced log loss relative to random retention by 0.03280 for R3 versus 0.00703 for R2. Removing the final 12 hours increased log loss relative to count-matched random removal by 0.01947 for R3 versus 0.00822 for R2. Under reduced availability, the local R3 increment changed from beneficial to harmful. Discussion: Physiological trajectories transferred more consistently, while observation-pattern features were particularly sensitive to the timing and availability of measurements. Conclusion: Clinical prediction models should be evaluated not only in new patient populations but also under the measurement conditions that supply their inputs.

title: Teva ends trial of one of its original line-up of innovative meds over futility
Clot waveform analysis in haemostatic and systemic disorders: current applications and clinical potential.
source: PubMed · Journal of thrombosis and thrombolysis
desc: [Journal of thrombosis and thrombolysis] Clot waveform analysis (CWA), originate from conventional coagulation assays, particularly the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and prothrombin time (PT), offers enhanced sensitivity and dynamic profiling of haemostatic processes. By capturing real-time changes in clot formation kinetics, CWA patterns provide disease specific changes beyond traditional clotting time. It has potential clinical utility in identifying bleeding risk in inherited and acquired bleeding disorders, as well as prothrombotic states in condition such as infections and myocardial infarction. A unique APTT second-derivative curves have been reported in COVID-19 infection. In malignancy, it may help clinicians to mitigate the risk of developing thrombotic complications due to cancer-associated hypercoagulability. This review covers the principles, analytical parameters, and clinical applications of CWA. As evidence continues to grow, integrating CWA into standard coagulation testing algorithms, particularly with the use of artificial intelligence, may potentially lead to improvements in patient stratification, monitoring and management in both acute and chronic haemostatic disorders.

title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
desc: Hundreds of millions of people now ask large language model (LLM) chatbots for health advice, which raises a question that is simple to pose and hard to answer: does everyone get the same advice? We audit six widely deployed LLMs from four providers on smoking cessation, a domain with codified clini- cal guidance and substantial public-health stakes, by putting the same four cessation questions to twelve user personas that differ in life stage, self-described expertise, and smoking history, for a total of 2,880 responses. What the models say depends on who appears to be asking. Every model named FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often to teen personas than to adult personas, by 32 to 67 percentage points, and in five of six models a persona presenting health- care expertise received fewer facts than a persona presenting none. We then evaluate one deployable intervention: a short system prompt specifying a factual floor, the set of core med- ical facts every user should receive when they are relevant, while leaving tone, vocabulary, and framing free to adapt. The prompt narrows persona differences in every model, but its effect on overall fact coverage varies in both magnitude and direction across models, so a prompt validated on one system cannot be assumed to transfer to another. Two cautions frame these results. Equal mention rates are not always the correct clinical target, because prescription cessation pharmacother- apy is not recommended for minors, so a defensible factual floor must be age-aware rather than uniform. And because our personas vary on several attributes at once, we report scenario- level differences rather than isolated effects of age or expertise. We release all 2,880 responses and the analysis code.

title: Karyopharm files Chapter 11, lines up Ayrmid as lead bidder in planned merger
Tryptophan metabolism within the gut-brain axis in depression: mechanisms, association with heterogeneity, and therapeutic opportunities.
desc: [Molecular psychiatry] Depression is a highly heterogeneous psychiatric disorder, characterized by substantial variability in clinical manifestations, treatment responses, and disease progression, thereby posing significant challenges to precision diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. Accumulating evidence indicates that dysregulated tryptophan metabolism, mediated through dynamic crosstalk with the gut microbiota and the gut-brain axis (GBA), plays a pivotal role in both the pathophysiology and biological heterogeneity of depression. In this review, we delineate the contributions of the three principal tryptophan metabolic pathways-the kynurenine, serotonin, and microbial indole pathways-in modulating neuroimmune signaling, neurotransmitter function, and gut-brain communication. Moreover, we synthesize current evidence demonstrating that microbiota-dependent tryptophan metabolism exhibits distinct profiles across clinical, demographic, immunometabolic, trauma-related, and genetically defined depressive phenotypes, thereby establishing its role as a unifying biological framework underlying depressive heterogeneity. We further provide a critical appraisal of emerging therapeutic strategies targeting microbiota-associated tryptophan metabolism, including pharmacological, nutritional, microbial, and traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions. Future investigations should integrate multi-omics approaches, longitudinal study designs, and mechanistic validation with artificial intelligence to elucidate causal relationships between microbiota-associated tryptophan metabolism and depressive heterogeneity, ultimately facilitating biomarker discovery and the development of precision therapeutics.

title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models
desc: Clinical trial failures are a major barrier to efficient drug development, incurring substantial costs and delaying patient access to effective therapies. Structured approaches such as the Hierarchical Interaction Network (HINT) predict trial outcomes by explicitly modelling interactions between drugs, diseases and protocols, but make limited use of the free text in trial registrations. We evaluate two domain-specific language models, BioBERT (108M parameters) and BioMistral (7B parameters), for phase-level outcome prediction on the TOP benchmark (12,477 trials), representing each trial as text built from ten ClinicalTrials.gov fields. We compare fine-tuning (full fine-tuning for BioBERT, low-rank adaptation for BioMistral) with probing, in which the pretrained model is frozen and only a lightweight classifier is trained on its embeddings. On the held-out test set of each phase, all four language-model variants achieved higher ROC-AUC (0.613--0.772) and PR-AUC (0.649--0.901) than the published HINT results, corresponding to relative PR-AUC gains of 10--20\%. F1 differences were small and mixed, and no model, including HINT, clearly exceeded the F1 of a trivial classifier that predicts success for every trial. Under the configurations tested, probing performed comparably to fine-tuning: fine-tuned models scored highest on ROC-AUC and PR-AUC in Phases I and II, and frozen BioMistral embeddings in Phase III (ROC-AUC 0.772; PR-AUC 0.901), although most differences between variants were below 0.03 and were not tested for significance. These results suggest that pretrained biomedical representations already encode signal relevant to trial outcome, and that probing is a computationally cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for this task.

title: Abbott
Artificial intelligence-assisted spectral microbiology for rapid microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction: advances, challenges, and future perspectives.
source: PubMed · Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease
desc: [Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease] Rapid microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction are fundamental to precision diagnostics, effective infection control, and antimicrobial stewardship. Artificial intelligence-assisted spectral microbiology is increasingly being investigated to convert complex spectral and imaging data into rapid microbiological identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction outputs. This review critically examines the integration of AI with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, Raman spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and automated colony imaging for microbial identification, strain discrimination, and AMR prediction. This work focuses on spectral preprocessing, feature engineering, machine-learning architectures, interpretability, validation, and clinical translation. Emerging evidence shows substantial potential to accelerate diagnostics while improving analytical precision and scalability. Nevertheless, dataset heterogeneity, instrument-dependent variability, limited external validation, and insufficient model transparency continue to constrain real-world adoption. Future integration of multimodal spectral, genomic, and clinical data could deliver robust, explainable, and interoperable diagnostic systems. It may support precision microbiology and antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, provided standardized acquisition, external validation, quality control, and uncertainty-aware interpretation are in place.

title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation
desc: LLM-based simulated interviewees support interviewer training and the evaluation of mental health interviewing systems. Existing studies have primarily focused on improving human-likeness through richer patient profiles and behavioral modeling. However, human-likeness alone does not establish their reliability. Reliable simulation requires preserving profile-grounded clinical facts (informational invariance) while adapting disclosure and interaction behavior to the interview (relational adaptivity). To this end, we introduce PsyInterviewee, which separates a protected truth channel from a dynamic interaction channel and verifies generated clinical claims against the profile. Specifically, asymmetric write permissions allow dialogue context to update disclosure and behavioral states without authorizing new clinical facts; these states guide what profile-supported information is revealed and how it is expressed. In an automated evaluation of interactions between LLM-based interviewers and interviewees, PsyInterviewee achieves higher scores than four representative baselines on most metrics across both axes, as assessed by two LLM judges. Ablations suggest that the two channels contribute to clinical grounding and response modulation, respectively.

title: Inizio
[Current advances and challenges of artificial intelligence in cervical spine surgery].
source: PubMed · Zhonghua yi xue za zhi
desc: [Zhonghua yi xue za zhi] Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded its applications in medicine, demonstrating potential in imaging analysis, risk prediction, and decision support. Owing to the complexity of disease patterns and the experience-dependent nature of clinical decision-making, AI holds considerable promise in cervical spine surgery. However, most existing studies remain focused on retrospective modeling and technical validation, with limited evidence supporting clinical usability and generalizability. From a clinically driven perspective, this review summarizes the major application scenarios and developmental trends of AI in cervical spine surgery, and highlights key challenges related to causal inference, data quality, multi-center collaboration, and legal and ethical considerations, aiming to provide a rational basis for the standardized application of AI in this field.

title: OntoDoc: Automatically Generating Ontology Resource Descriptions
desc: Knowledge graphs and ontologies form the backbone of structured, machine-readable knowledge representation, yet ontology terms often lack natural language descriptions, limiting their accessibility and reuse. Existing ontology verbalization approaches tend to rely on rule-based or template-driven techniques that operate on strict, formal schema axioms, resulting in rigid verbalizations that fail to convey richer contextual semantics. We present OntoDoc, a multi-agent framework for automatically generating natural language descriptions for any Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) within a SPARQL endpoint or RDF file. OntoDoc operates through a four-stage pipeline: (1) a Database Context agent that adaptively explores the knowledge graph via SPARQL to collect semantically informative triples about the target IRI; (2) a Web Context agent that retrieves and re-ranks encyclopedic background knowledge from Wikipedia and the open web; (3) an Assumption Generation agent that synthesizes both contexts into a structured, evidence-grounded list of intermediate assumptions; and (4) a Description Generation agent that produces the final natural language description from the grounded assumptions. We evaluate OntoDoc on three knowledge graphs spanning biomedical, agricultural, and cross-domain settings, using both automatic scoring via Large Language Models (LLMs) and human evaluation with 11 annotators. OntoDoc consistently matches or exceeds a naive LLM baseline and a template-based ontology verbalizer in accuracy. Furthermore, it vastly outperforms both baselines in the completeness of the generated descriptions, delivering an average 12% improvement in completeness over the naive baseline across all domains, and improving completeness scores by as much as 2.8 points on a 5-point scale relative to the ontology verbalizer.

title: MD Live by Evernorth
Chemistry-transforming applications of artificial intelligence.
desc: [Chemical Society reviews] Artificial intelligence is increasingly used across chemical research, but its practical value depends on where it intervenes in the workflow and how reliably it generalizes beyond curated benchmarks. This review adopts a pipeline-based perspective: we first decompose chemical research into stages that generate, transform, and validate information and then map AI methods onto these stages with an emphasis on measurable outcomes and failure modes. We summarize classical machine learning and emerging chemistry-informed and foundation model approaches, highlighting recurrent pitfalls such as data leakage, overfitting, and extrapolation. We then critically survey applications spanning knowledge extraction, experimental data interpretation (including data from spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and microscopy), property and reactivity prediction, synthesis planning, and closed-loop experimentation, focusing on representative case studies that illustrate transferable design patterns rather than exhaustive coverage. Across these domains, the evidence supports a shift from static structure-property thinking toward dynamic, data-rich decision cycles where models prioritize experiments, extract mechanistic descriptors from complex signals, and guide iterative refinement under constraints. We conclude by outlining requirements for robust deployment and discussing near-term directions for chemistry-grounded foundation models and intelligent experimental platforms.

title: Capacity Planning for Resource-Constrained Clinical LLM Serving
desc: Deploying large language models (LLMs) under a fixed accelerator budget requires jointly deciding how computational capacity is allocated across model sizes and how incoming requests are routed across that capacity. Although prior work has extensively studied LLM routing and serving efficiency, the relative importance of fleet composition and routing under resource constraints remains less understood. We investigate this question using a controlled four-GPU serving environment with heterogeneous clinical NLP workloads spanning short factual verification, biomedical semantic matching, and long-context clinical summarization. We systematically vary fleet composition, routing policy, and offered load while holding the workload trace and hardware budget fixed. Across 24 configurations, descriptive main-effect shares attribute more variation to fleet composition than to the evaluated routing policies in time to first token, latency, and long-context coverage. All-small fleets provide the best responsiveness and throughput but substantially lower long-context coverage, whereas larger-model capacity improves coverage at the cost of serving efficiency. Heterogeneous fleets provide intermediate operating points but can introduce strong-model bottlenecks when large-model capacity is scarce. In a focused evaluation of this bottleneck, capacity-aware routing reduces mean latency and increases throughput while incurring a small reduction in long-context coverage. Within this measured regime, the results support prioritizing capacity allocation, with routing managing demand within the provisioned capacity.

title: Building on the 2025 National Academies Pharmacy Workshop: Preparing Pharmacists for Technology-Driven Roles.
source: PubMed · American journal of pharmaceutical education
desc: [American journal of pharmaceutical education] To identify the competencies that pharmacists need to evaluate, implement, and oversee technology-enabled care and propose a longitudinal framework for developing these competencies within PharmD education. Drawing on the 2025 National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) Pharmacy Workshop, this paper links emerging technologies to new pharmacist roles across clinical, regulatory, managed care, and industry settings. The new technologies demand that pharmacists validate artificial intelligence (AI) recommendations, implement digital therapeutics, apply pharmacogenomic (PGx) data, and interpret real-world evidence (RWE), all of which extend beyond traditional pharmacotherapy training. We propose four longitudinally scaffolded domains: Technical Understanding, Critical Evaluation, Ethical and Professional Stewardship, and Discipline-Specific Application. Technology is not diminishing the pharmacist's role. Rather, it highlights the importance of pharmacists' clinical expertise. Preparing graduates requires deliberate curricular design, faculty investment, and recognition that clinical judgment remains the irreplaceable complement to any algorithm.

title: CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports
desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promise for chest radiograph report generation, but adoption remains limited because of hallucinated findings that are not grounded in the image. Correcting these hallucinations and improving overall report quality remains a significant challenge. Prior work has addressed this problem by refining models with reinforcement learning, preference optimization, or chain-of-thought supervision, often at substantial compute cost. To address this gap, we introduce CheXPoT, a program-of-thought (PoT) framework that verifies each generated finding against image features and removes those it cannot ground. CheXPoT decomposes generated reports into predicates with RadGraph and an LLM, grounds these predicates against a DenseNet-121 and Grad-CAM visual evidence table, executes PoT verification code, and rewrites reports after removing unsupported predicates. On a 4,145-image held-out split, CheXPoT yields statistically significant precision gains on 8 of 14 CheXpert classes and F1 gains on 5, with no significant decreases in either metric. CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 19.2% (MedGemma-4B) to 46.8% (MedGemma-4B + CheXPoT) and micro-average F1 from 23.0% to 49.4%, absolute gains of 27.6% and 26.4% respectively. We also tested CheXPoT on other VLM report generators. On LLaVA-Med, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 4.5% to 17.7% and micro-average F1 from 6.3% to 19.4%. On MAIRA-2, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 15.6% to 42.1% and micro-average F1 from 21.0% to 45.3%. Our results suggest that inexpensive post-hoc visual verification may improve VLM trustworthiness by correcting unsupported findings from generated reports. CheXPoT lays a foundation for tools that help validate VLM-generated radiology reports and reduce unsupported findings. These innovations may subsequently help increase trust and adoption of VLM tools in Medicine.

title: Harnessing big data and artificial intelligence for personalized medicine: from multi-omics integration to clinical decision-making.
desc: [Personalized medicine] High-throughput technologies generate large and complex biological datasets that can challenge conventional methods of analysis and visualization. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support the analysis and integration of these datasets, provide new analytical approaches, and accelerate biological research. However, reliable AI applications depend on high-quality, consistent data. Technical errors, bias, and deficiencies in analytical methods can produce misleading findings and undermine reproducibility. AI-based approaches may help identify errors and improve data quality, but poor-quality or biased datasets, limited reproducibility, and concerns about privacy and ethics remain important barriers to their use in biological research. A literature search was performed in PubMed for papers published between 2015 and 2025. This review summarizes recent advances in AI for biological data analysis, including its main applications and potential benefits. It also discusses methodological, translational, and ethical challenges that may limit implementation. Particular attention is given to data quality and reliability, alongside the responsible use of AI in biological research and its translation to personalized medicine.

title: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings
desc: Dimension reduction methods are chosen by a common claim: t-SNE and UMAP preserve local structure, and PCA preserves global structure. Checking it on given data takes local and global scores on one scale and a test that compares two maps. Both scores come from one curve. The locality profile is the chance-corrected share of each point's k nearest neighbors that a map keeps, over all neighborhood sizes. Its value at k = 10 is the local fidelity L, and its mean over 30 to 50 percent of the data is the global fidelity G. We prove that at the midpoint the profile is the agreement on which half of the data is near each point, a rank correlation of the distances. Because L and G are one statistic, two maps can be tested against each other. The LG reversal test applies to any two dimension reduction methods. It decides, with a block-jackknife p-value, whether one map is more local and the other more global, and returns the scale at which to change maps. On 156 maps of twelve datasets with up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.89 and 0.96, and 2,000 points estimate it. The test confirms the usual claim on seven datasets. On both retail datasets and both rolled-up manifolds, it finds the neighbor embeddings more global. In an agent memory of one million passages, the two maps cross at 150,000 passages (p = 2.6e-5). Applications span pathology, single cells, supply chains and AI agent memory.

title: Autonomic nervous system dysfunction in critically ill cancer patients: Hemodynamic consequences and multimodal assessment strategies.
desc: [Cancer pathogenesis and therapy] In critically ill cancer patients, autonomic nervous system (ANS) dysfunction may contribute to hemodynamic instability and organ dysfunction and may be exacerbated by malignancy-related injury and anticancer treatment. This narrative review summarizes conventional methods for assessing ANS function, including heart rate variability (HRV), blood pressure variability (BPV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and cardiovascular autonomic reflex testing, together with emerging approaches such as high-resolution multimodal monitoring (MMM) and artificial intelligence (AI). Host-organ unregulated response (HOUR) framework is used to integrate interactions among autonomic, neuroendocrine, inflammatory, immune, coagulation, metabolic, bioenergetic, and microcirculatory dysregulation. Collectively, these approaches may facilitate real-time assessment of autonomic function and tissue perfusion, thereby supporting risk stratification and individualized management in critically ill cancer patients.

title: Accurate and Auditable ECG Classification via Visibility Graph Neural Networks
desc: Physicians read electrocardiograms (ECGs) from waveform shape and timing, yet accurate deep-learning classifiers rarely show which waveform regions drive their predictions. We introduce LYNX-ECG, a graph neural network that represents each heartbeat as a sparse visibility graph of timestamped turning points. On CODE-Test, LYNX-ECG reaches a macro F1 score of 0.889, outperforming five baselines including the ECGFounder foundation model, while its graphs need about 14% of the storage of graphs built from every sample. Because each node maps to a specific ECG time, we can delete clinically defined waveform regions and alter beat timing to audit predictions. For conduction disorders, the clinically expected region was the strongest evidence in more than 90% of correct predictions. Bradycardia and tachycardia calls follow heart rate with conduction intervals held fixed, and atrial fibrillation calls vanish when beat-to-beat variation is removed. Sparse visibility graphs thus pair accurate ECG classification with clinically grounded, testable explanations.

title: AI Literacy as a Leadership Competency: Preparing Nurse Executives for Artificial Intelligence Governance.
source: PubMed · The Journal of nursing administration
desc: [The Journal of nursing administration] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly integrating into health care delivery, influencing clinical, operational, and strategic decision-making. Nurse executives must therefore possess competencies that enable informed oversight of AI-enabled systems. This article proposes an AI literacy competency framework for nurse executive practice, adapted from existing AI literacy scholarship and aligned with nursing leadership responsibilities. The framework provides a conceptual foundation for integrating AI literacy into leadership competency development, translating theoretical constructs into practice that is aligned with executive decision-making. The framework also defines knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary for ethical governance, evaluation, and responsible implementation of AI in health care organizations. In doing so, it offers a structured approach for preparing nurse leaders to guide the responsible adoption and oversight of AI-enabled technologies.

title: VariaFlow: Uncertainty-Aware Flow Matching for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
desc: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection no longer fails at reconstruction. Generative models produce high-quality pseudo-healthy reconstructions, and the remaining difficulty is the step of scoring residuals. The residual between a scan and its reconstruction has two indistinguishable sources, genuine pathology and the anatomical variation that separates one healthy brain from another. Scoring against a single reconstruction treats both as anomalous, inflating false positives where healthy anatomy varies most while small or subtle lesions are lost in the surrounding reconstruction error. We identify the missing quantity as the predictive variance, how much a healthy reconstruction can vary at each location. We introduce VariaFlow, which estimates this variance from an ensemble of mask-guided restorations under an unconditional flow matching prior, each started from a different noise initialization, and which normalizes the residual by the resulting standard deviation. Few-step flow matching keeps the ensemble computationally affordable, and restoring at two spatial scales captures lesions of different size. Across three brain MRI datasets spanning stroke and tumor, VariaFlow is trained once on healthy anatomy and generalizes across all three, attaining the highest AUROC (0.94, 0.80, 0.78) on each and the highest AUPRC on both cross-domain datasets, exceeding the strongest baseline by 37% and 50%. Under domain shift, the same baseline drops by up to 52% in AUPRC, whereas VariaFlow stays more stable and achieves the best small-lesion Dice on all three datasets.

title: Evolution of diagnostic reference levels in paediatric cardiac interventional procedures: a narrative review.
source: PubMed · Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
desc: [Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine] The goal of this narrative review was to identify and synthesise publications reporting radiation dose values for paediatric cardiac interventional procedures (PCIP), organised according to four DRL-related benchmarking levels used in this review: typical values, local DRLs, national DRLs and regional DRLs. These procedures can deliver high radiation doses to markedly radiosensitive patients. DRLs are an important tool for optimising these exposures. Publications from 2010 to 2025 were searched, and twenty-five studies met the eligibility criteria, with reported kerma-area product (PKA) taken as a common comparator. Reported PKA spanned more than two orders of magnitude, from below 1 Gy cm2 in patients under 5 kg to above 100 Gy cm2 for complex therapeutic procedures in larger children. Within a single DRL category, procedural complexity alone drove differences exceeding one order of magnitude, while procedure-specific stratification converged on a narrow 1-5 Gy cm2 band in the youngest patients. National DRLs showed the widest inter-study dispersion and regional DRLs the narrowest. The variability in reported dose values was primarily driven by differences in categorisation schemes and procedural complexity rather than by inconsistencies in the DRL concept itself. The available evidence reflects an evolution from early local initiatives towards national and regional frameworks characterised by increasing methodological maturity and international collaboration. Future developments are expected to move towards complexity-based DRLs supported by large multicentre datasets, automated dose monitoring and artificial intelligence for real-time optimisation, while coordinated regional initiatives and shared registries may enable continuous DRL updating and stronger radiation protection for PCIP.

title: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification
desc: Chronic kidney disease is characterized by structural alterations in renal tissue and progressive loss of kidney function. While glomerular subtype ratios provide a compact and clinically meaningful summary of glomerular composition, representing pathomic information using whole-slide image (WSI)-level mean values diminishes glomerulus-level heterogeneity and the contribution of less prevalent patterns. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated whether modeling individual glomeruli using multiple-instance learning (MIL) could provide complementary information to conventional subtype ratios for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classification. We analyzed 162 kidney-biopsy WSIs from 162 patients, categorizing renal function as eGFR = 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Quantitative size, shape, intensity, and texture features were extracted from segmented glomeruli, representing each patient as a bag of glomerular instances. An attention-based MIL model was trained to aggregate these heterogeneous pathomic profiles. We evaluated subtype ratios, pathomics, and their combination using ABMIL, with a mean-pooled multilayer perceptron baseline. In five-fold cross-validation, the subtype-ratio-only model achieved an AUC of 0.7262 +/- 0.0596. MIL using pathomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.7362 +/- 0.0788, whereas integrating pathomics with subtype ratios produced the highest mean AUC of 0.7630 +/- 0.0665. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine individual feature contributions. These results demonstrate that MIL-based pathomics can complement established glomerular subtype ratios by capturing additional glomerulus-level information for quantitative kidney-biopsy analysis.

title: Machine Learning in the Differential Diagnosis of Bipolar and Borderline Personality Disorders: A Scoping Review.
source: PubMed · Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
desc: [Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie] BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) are associated with substantial morbidity and can be difficult to distinguish when symptoms are assessed cross-sectionally. This scoping review examines machine learning (ML) and related predictive approaches designed to differentiate the two conditions.MethodsWe searched Ovid MEDLINE, APA PsycInfo, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and selected computer science conference proceedings through July 2, 2026. Full-text peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers were eligible when they used a data-driven computational or statistical prediction approach to distinguish, classify, or characterize BD and BPD. Of 2,594 records identified, 2,523 unique records were screened, and 24 full texts were assessed. Screening followed the Population, Concept, Context framework, Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, and preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses extension for scoping reviews.ResultsNine reports met the inclusion criteria. Seven participant-based reports contributed an aggregate of 986 report-level participants, although two reports used overlapping cohorts; one conference paper used synthetic data, and one study analyzed 149,798 Reddit posts. Studies including clinical samples reported BD versus BPD discrimination AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) values of 0.67 to 0.91 and accuracies ranging from 61.7% to 90%. These estimates were not directly comparable and were derived from small, often imbalanced samples using heterogeneous internal validation. No model was externally validated in an independent clinical cohort.ConclusionThe evidence remains preliminary and does not support clinical deployment. Reported performance is constrained by small samples, class imbalance, uncertain ground-truth labels, spectrum bias, and reliance on pre-existing diagnoses. Prospective studies in consecutive at-risk cohorts, with transparent reporting and independent external validation, are required.

title: MedAstra: ASR-less Speech Retrieval with Diagnostic Grounding for Medical QA
desc: Spoken medical question answering can fail when automatic speech recognition (ASR) corrupts a clinically important term before retrieval. We present MedAstra, a framework that maps frozen WavLM speech representations through a lightweight adapter into a frozen E5 text embedding space. This enables a dense retrieval path that accepts a waveform without a query transcript. Retrieved passages and speech-linked textual metadata support answer generation with entity alternatives, diagnostic contrasts, relation heuristics, and bounded retrieval refinement. ASR-less refers to the initial speech retrieval interface; lexical retrieval, string-based entity correction, and the text generator require textual inputs. The deterministic speech embedding does not constitute a calibrated model of acoustic uncertainty. Reported retrieval results reach 87.6 Recall@10 for the speech-only retriever and 90.4 for the hybrid configuration, compared with 81.0 for transcript-first dense retrieval. Medical QA and ablations provide descriptive system comparisons, with input-provenance and evaluation limitations stated explicitly. We distinguish controlled synthetic acoustic tests from real clinical speech, qualify component attribution, and specify the remaining comparisons needed to assess speech-only QA and clinical generalization.

title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research
desc: [Journal of medical Internet research] Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.

title: CuPH: Parallel Cubical Persistent Homology via Level-Synchronous Component Tracking
desc: Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook. Standard cubical PH decomposes an image into cubical cells (vertices, edges, and squares) and reduces them sequentially in filtration order. This sequential reduction has $Θ(n)$ parallel depth for an $n$-pixel image, limiting within-image GPU parallelism and constraining its use in topology-aware deep learning. We introduce CuPH, a GPU-based parallel algorithm for computing cubical PH on 2D images that operates directly on pixels rather than cubical cells. CuPH buckets pixels by filtration values, activates them with a level-synchronous sweep, and tracks connected components with a lock-free union-find method. We prove that CuPH produces persistence diagrams identical to standard cubical PH on integer inputs, with a stability bound for floating-point inputs. CuPH reduces parallel depth from $Θ(n)$ to $O(L\log n)$ for an image with $L$ intensity levels. We implement the level sweep as a single CUDA kernel, eliminating cross-level kernel-launch overhead. Empirically, CuPH is $18.6$--$99.6\times$ faster than the existing GPU baseline (CMP). As a drop-in PH backend, CuPH accelerates topology-aware classification ($4.2$--$16.7\times$) and segmentation ($8.3$--$44\times$) while preserving accuracy. It also enables computing full-image PH losses on high-resolution images, improving segmentation Dice by $2.2$--$4.6$ points over patch-local PH baselines and accelerating training by $25$--$31\times$.

title: AI-Guided Intrinsic and Extrinsic Photocorrosion Inhibition of III-V Semiconductors for Durable Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting.
desc: [Small science] Group III-V semiconductors are suitable for solar-driven hydrogen production due to precise lattice matching (for tandem device combinations), high carrier mobilities (>103 cm2 V-1 s-1), tunable bandgaps (1.1-2.5 eV), strong absorption coefficients (>105 cm-1), and a large range of doping possibilities. GaInP2, GaAs, and InP have a theoretical solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of more than 20%. Still, their high susceptibility to chemical and photochemical corrosion during prolonged photoelectrochemical water splitting (PEC-WS) is a major industrial hurdle. This review comprehensively covers critical strategies to enhance the photostability of group III-V semiconductors for industrial-scale PEC-WS, emphasizing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) support. We discuss three main intrinsic and extrinsic strategies that include (i) AI-driven crystal structure modification and faceted growth control, (ii) physical and chemical surface passivation coupled with machine learning for passivation material screening strategies, and (iii) combining III-V semiconductors with appropriate band-aligned materials via preferable heterojunctions, utilizing algorithms to select optimal compositions. We examine the underlying mechanisms of each strategy and conclude with perspectives on achieving optimal materials for PEC-WS using advanced AI and ML screening tools. Implementing these effective modification strategies, the wide commercial potential of III-V photoelectrodes for PEC-WS technology can be unlocked.

title: HALO: Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records
desc: Learning from extensive longitudinal clinical records--spanning repeated encounters, evolving conditions, and heterogeneous documentation--under a finite labeling budget requires solving two coupled problems: deciding what evidence to keep and deciding which patients deserve higher-fidelity labels. Prior work on active learning and multi-fidelity label acquisition mainly addresses the second problem, while treating the evidence presented to the acquisition policy as fixed. We present HALO, a Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning pipeline for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records. This framework jointly learns what to read and what label source to acquire under budget. HALO first selects informative evidence from longitudinal records and then uses a budget-aware policy to allocate free-, silver-, and gold-fidelity label sources. For frozen policies, our theory characterizes asymmetric acquired-label channels and gives a budget-constrained finite-sample gold-risk bound for a common downstream logistic model. In a heart-failure case study, HALO attained the highest MedAlign acquired-label F1 at six of eight target budgets. A downstream classifier trained on HALO-acquired labels attained the highest external MGB F1 at budgets 15-60 and remained within 0.01 of the best comparator at budgets 75-120.

title: AI algorithms and external validation: promises, pitfalls, and a practical blueprint.
desc: [European heart journal] External validation involving the testing of a frozen AI model on independent data from other sites, populations, time periods, or devices provides the clearest estimate of intended-use setting performance when those external data are deployment-representative of the expected population, measurement processes, and clinical workflow. It yields realistic estimates of discrimination and calibration, exposes shortcut learning and distribution shift, quantifies clinical utility through decision-analytic measures, and reveals subgroup disparities requiring mitigation. Yet common pitfalls undermine credibility: quasi-external splits with hidden relatedness; spectrum and prevalence mismatch; site, workflow, and hardware effects; label noise and reference-standard drift; analytic flexibility and selective reporting; small, underpowered samples; reliance only on the area under the curve; unreported threshold tuning; and leakage. A practical blueprint emphasizes pre-registration; representative, multi-site cohorts spanning geography, time, and acquisition; prevention of patient and temporal overlap; comprehensive evaluation of discrimination, calibration (including calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and calibration plots), and net benefit with confidence intervals; pre-specified subgroup and fairness audits; transparent labelling procedures and uncertainty analyses; principled sample-size calculations; and minimal, well-documented model updating (recalibration before revision). Finally, external validation should connect to post-deployment governance via drift detection, performance triggers, and change-control plans, complemented by site-specific local evaluation to ensure safety and reliability across diverse clinical environments. When executed to these standards, external validation transforms promising prototypes into dependable clinical tools, clarifying where a model performs, where it fails, and what adaptations are necessary for safe, equitable, and sustainable use. This framework links statistical evaluation to clinical use, model updating, and post-deployment monitoring.

title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
desc: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: https://magnusdtd.github.io/CoreCalib/ .

title: Global Virology Meets the Viruses of the Changing World: Where Ecology, Evolution, One Health, Artificial Intelligence, and Innovation Unite to Decode Viruses.
desc: [Virusdisease] This article highlights the current issue of VirusDisease in the fast-changing scenario of modern virology and introduces the VIROCON 2026, the flagship national conference of the Indian Virological Society, which will be held in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, on 11-13 November 2026 with the theme "Viruses in the ChangingWorld: Ecology, Evolution and Future Preparedness." The current issue covers the wide range of contemporary virological research, including molecular and structural virology, emerging and re-emerging viruses, diagnostics, computational methods, epidemiology, co-infections, and viral evolution. VIROCON 2026 builds on this interdisciplinary perspective with eight thematic tracks that combine One Health, AI, metagenomics, ecology, climate change, therapeutics, vaccines, and preparedness. The issue and conference highlight the need for collaboration, innovation, and globally connected virology to prepare for and address future viral threats.

title: Where Does EEG Help Wearable Freezing of Gait Detection?
desc: Freezing of gait (FoG) detectors built on inertial measurement units (IMUs) are accurate while the legs move, but they become unreliable when the legs are nearly still, which is exactly when akinetic freezing, voluntary stopping, and standing must be told apart. Electroencephalography (EEG) captures motor-planning activity that leg sensors cannot, but EEG is impractical for daily use. We ask where EEG helps: as an input at inference time, or only during pretraining, so that the deployed detector still needs only IMUs. We assemble a pretraining corpus of synchronized EEG and IMU recordings (5 datasets, 184 people, 94 hours) and compare six settings that differ only in the modalities used for pretraining and as model input, each with tuned hyperparameters and five independent pretraining runs. On the BXHC FoG dataset (leave-one-patient-out, 10 patients with FoG), adding EEG as input raises FoG F1 from 0.663 to 0.740 (9 of 10 patients improve), and the gain in ranking performance is confined to the quartile of windows with the least leg movement (AUROC +0.063). Pretraining the IMU encoder jointly with EEG improves an IMU-only detector both within the cohort (FoG F1 0.663 to 0.705) and when it is trained on a small cohort and tested on another (FoG F1 +0.083, all 10 test patients improve). Repeating the study with PD-only and healthy-only pretraining corpora, each with its own hyperparameter search, shows that IMU-based detection is robust to the corpus, whereas the benefit of aligning EEG with IMU requires both. Cross-cohort analysis further shows that detectors trained without annotated voluntary stops classify nearly all stops as freezing. Finally, on PD versus non-PD classification in three external datasets, joint EEG+IMU pretraining improves PD detection from walking EEG over EEG-only pretraining (AUROC 0.750 vs. 0.683), while IMU-based detection does not depend on the pretraining.

title: Authenticity across human and synthetic influencers: a configurational review of source evaluation and social influence.
desc: [Frontiers in psychology] Authenticity has become a central concern in social media influencer research, yet its construction is examined differently across human, virtual, and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated sources. This study examines how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across these influencer contexts. This study conducted a corpus-based review of 1,676 English-language research articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus between July 2017 and March 2026. BERTopic modeling was employed to identify recurring semantic topics, followed by an abductive, theory-informed synthesis organized around source ontology and the dominant basis of authenticity construction. Temporal changes in relative topic prevalence were examined across the eight complete calendar years from 2018 to 2025. The synthesis identified four configurations: relational human authenticity, curated human authenticity, humanized synthetic authenticity, and governed synthetic authenticity. Human-influencer research emphasizes biography, accumulated interaction, commercial congruence, and motive transparency, whereas synthetic-influencer research places greater weight on persona coherence, humanization, identity disclosure, ownership, automation, and accountability. Credibility, trust, parasocial interaction, social presence, and engagement emerge as closely associated evaluative processes. Temporal analysis revealed selective changes in relative topic prevalence, particularly concerning virtual-influencer credibility, humanization, and tourism-related applications, while most topics showed no clear linear trend. The findings provide a corpus- and method-dependent framework for understanding how authenticity is constructed and evaluated across human and synthetic influencer contexts. The framework highlights distinct evidential foundations underlying authenticity judgments and offers a basis for further research on source evaluation and social influence.

title: Ensemble Classification and Cancer-Specific Gene Signatures from Quality-Aware Hybrid Gene Selection in TCGA RNA-Seq data
desc: Gene-expression classifiers of cancer type are usually developed and validated within one cohort using random splits. Starting from a quality-aware hybrid Boruta selector from earlier work, we developed and evaluated ensemble classifiers and cancer-specific gene signatures. Using 10,469 TCGA tumours of 33 types, we compared five learners and three ensembles under decision rules fixed in advance, reran the selection in site-grouped cross-validation, transferred a breast-cancer subtype panel to 3273 tumours of the independent SCAN-B cohort, and built five-gene stage~I tumour versus adjacent-normal panels for nine cancer types. Logistic regression (LR) was the most accurate and best-calibrated single learner (balanced accuracy 0.943 on the locked test set). Stacking added at most 0.006 with 1000 genes but improved on LR in every fold with a minimal 100-gene panel; a hierarchical model did not reduce within-group confusion. Site-grouped validation lowered balanced accuracy by 0.027, almost entirely in colon and rectal cancer (0.008 without them and the untestable LAML). On SCAN-B, the subtype panel reached 0.855, close to the 50 PAM50 genes (0.876). Stage~I panels reached ROC AUC >= 0.99 in held-out patients and detected most later-stage tumours. Ensembles help most with a minimal panel; with 1000 genes, a calibrated linear model suffices.

title: Colorimetric sensor arrays and artificial intelligence for natural product quality evaluation: From cross-reactive fingerprints to analytical validation.
desc: [Talanta] Natural products encompass traditional Chinese medicines, herbal medicines, teas, food-derived plant materials, plant extracts, and naturally occurring bioactive compounds. Their rapid identification and quality evaluation require a balance among integrative characterization, analytical accuracy, and field accessibility. Empirical authentication methods are difficult to quantify and reproduce, whereas confirmatory techniques based on chromatography, mass spectrometry, and spectroscopy, although analytically reliable, cannot fully meet the frequent demands of on-site screening, process monitoring, and risk triage. A colorimetric sensor array (CSA) generates sample-specific color fingerprints through cross-reactive responses across multiple sensing elements. Combined with standardized image acquisition, feature extraction, and chemometric or machine-learning analysis, CSA-based workflows can support classification, quantitative prediction, and anomaly detection. This integrated strategy is referred to here as CSA-AI, an umbrella term that does not equate conventional chemometrics with artificial intelligence (AI). This review critically examines CSA design, color-data acquisition, chemometric and AI-assisted analysis, analytical validation, and applications in natural product quality evaluation along the chain of "array response-color fingerprint-computational interpretation-quality decision-making." Particular attention is given to authentic complex matrices, sample-level data partitioning, data leakage, independently sourced external evaluation, cross-device transfer, validation evidence, model interpretability, and confirmation by established analytical methods. Current direct visible-CSA evidence is strongest for authentication and preliminary adulteration screening, whereas process monitoring, storage-deterioration warning, and field deployment remain less thoroughly validated. Current evidence supports CSA-AI primarily as a complementary tool for rapid screening, risk warning, and auxiliary grading rather than as a replacement for confirmatory methods such as HPLC, GC-MS, and LC-MS.

title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
desc: Radiologists' visual attention can supervise medical image learning, but how reader panel composition affects its value remains untested. We evaluated GazeRIB (Gaze-guided Radiologist-Informed Blackout), which masks unviewed regions during training and uses unmasked images at inference. Eight experts repeatedly read the same 80 chest X-rays (CXRs). We compared individual readers with three-, five- and eight-reader panels across seven architectures and 10 seeds, evaluating 910 models on a separate 2,897-CXR cohort for four-class severity prediction. Every panel improved macro F1 over the no-gaze baseline by 5.33-7.47 percentage points (pp; Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.007); no individual reader reached significance on this endpoint. Three readers captured 73-80% of the eight-reader gain in macro F1, the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AU-PRC). On external validation without retraining, all four panels improved ROC-AUC on SIIM-FISABIO-RSNA by +1.93 to +4.24 pp (p <= 0.004); on MIMIC-Eye no panel differed significantly from baseline, whereas the single-reader average declined (-1.40 pp, p = 0.008). Reader composition therefore influenced performance, although transfer depended on the cohort.

title: Unit-Area Optimized Flexible Triboelectric Nanogenerators for High-Performance Human Motion Sensing With Deep Learning.
source: PubMed · Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany)
desc: [Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany)] Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have garnered significant attention as self-powered energy harvesters and sensors, yet their performance critically depends on structural design and material engineering. In this work, we introduce a structured TENG designed with the concept of unit-area to maximize contact efficiency by minimizing mechanical interference between neighboring structures. Synergistically, barium titanate (BaTiO3) nanoparticles were incorporated into the elastomer matrix to enhance the dielectric constant and surface charge density. Based on this approach, unit-area-based TENGs (UA-TENGs) with various geometries were comprehensively evaluated through computational analysis and experimental validation. The results reveal that smaller structures enable more effective contact, while dome structures exhibit superior output compared to pyramid structures. Quantitatively, the optimized dome-structured UA-TENG with the BaTiO3 composite achieves a power density of 18 W/m2, a maximum voltage of 254 V, and enhanced pressure sensitivities. The device successfully powered 127 LEDs and operated small electronics. Furthermore, the UA-TENG demonstrated excellent performance in detecting biomechanical signals. Integration into a smart glove enabled real-time gesture recognition, where a convolutional neural network accurately classified five distinct hand motions to achieve reliable wireless drone control. These results demonstrate the broad application prospects of the UA-TENG in wearable energy supply, intelligent sensing, and human-machine interaction.

title: Does Vendor Image Processing Matter? Learning Echocardiography Display Appearance from Native Beamspace Data
desc: Most echocardiography datasets contain vendor-processed images, but processing is often undocumented and may affect model performance and robustness. To address this, we train a small convolutional neural network to reproduce General Electric display appearance from native beamspace brightness-mode ultrasound, using 8 406 recordings from 605 unique patients. The beamspace CNN reduces test mean absolute error by 43% over the optimal pointwise brightness map, outperforms an equivalent Cartesian CNN and runs in real time on a CPU. Across the EchoXFlow and CAMUS datasets, unfiltered training followed by filtered evaluation yields the lowest mean Dice for every class, suggesting filtering may be useful as augmentation when evaluation data are filtered or their processing is unknown. Code and pretrained weights: https://github.com/Ahus-AIM/EchoAppearance

title: How Does Digital Innovation Drive Corporate Sustainability? A Systematic Literature Review.
desc: [F1000Research] This study systematically reviews recent empirical evidence on the relationship between digital innovation and corporate sustainability. Using the Scopus database, the review identified 231 articles through the search string ("digital" OR "digital innovation" OR "digitalization") AND "corporate sustainability". After applying inclusion criteria covering publications from 2023 to 2026, English-language journal articles, open access availability, and quantitative empirical design, 49 articles were retained for synthesis. The findings show that digital innovation is conceptualized through multiple forms, including digital transformation, digital finance, artificial intelligence, digital accounting, supply chain digitalization, digital leadership, executives' digital attention, and digital-green integration. Most studies indicate that digital innovation positively contributes to ESG performance, corporate sustainability performance, sustainable development performance, and sustainability efficiency. However, the relationship is not automatic or universally linear. Its effect depends on mediating mechanisms such as green innovation, operational efficiency, financing access, information transparency, supply chain coordination, resource orchestration, and governance improvement. The review also identifies important boundary conditions, including digital maturity, organizational capability, leadership support, digital infrastructure, environmental regulation, and institutional quality. This study contributes by organizing fragmented empirical evidence into an integrated thematic framework and highlighting future research directions for global scholars examining digital transformation, ESG practices, and sustainability-oriented corporate strategy worldwide.

title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
desc: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study. It combines measurements of data relationships with two comparisons: changing the evaluation population while holding predictions fixed, and changing training data while holding evaluation fixed. Byte-identical files cross the public training-validation boundary, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings that contribute frames occur in both partitions. Shared source recordings establish cross-split overlap; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent counting unique shared patients. Across ten paired seeds, removing all training rows attributed to Kvasir-Capsule, plus five rows from other sources flagged as near-matches to it, lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%. Evaluating the same fitted models on the validation rows of the other sources reverses the comparison: removal improves balanced accuracy by 1.38 percentage points. The public-validation drop measures sensitivity to source removal, not an amount of leakage-induced inflation. Matched controls show that sample size and class counts alone do not explain the observed score differences. An exploratory experiment removes the training neighbors of validation frames that have close training matches, or equally many distant training rows, and yields a difference-in-differences estimate, relative to matched unflagged frames, of -0.355 percentage points in true-class probability; the paired-t interval for accuracy spans zero. The resulting procedure distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity and specifies the population, class support and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.
